anomalies_root_cause_explanation.why_720p_20s_was_faster_than_10s_in_p5_6: In P5.6.2, _generate_fast_test_clip used raw FFmpeg testsrc2 without scrolling. _is_static_around samples 5 timestamps [0.15d, 0.35d, 0.55d, 0.75d, 0.92d]. At d=10s ([1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5, 9.2]s), testsrc2's periodic sweeping bar crossed the bottom-right ring on one sample -> static_bg=False (mode='per_frame', 26.46s). At d=20s ([3.0, 7.0, 11.0, 15.0, 18.4]s, spaced by multiples of 4.0s), all 5 samples missed the sweeping bar in the bottom-right corner -> static_bg=True (mode='static_patch', computing SHIFTMAP once and blending in 14.95s), while the old script hardcoded mode='per_frame'.
anomalies_root_cause_explanation.why_1080p_10s_stood_around_62s_across_1_: Two exact root causes: (1) SlowAPI default_limits=['60/minute'] in backend/app/main.py applied to GET /api/v1/flow-cleanup/status/{job_id}, and because TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS was unset, get_client_ip ignored X-Forwarded-For and mapped all 1, 2, or 3 concurrent client threads to 127.0.0.1. Polling GET /status/{job_id} every 0.4s (2.5 req/s/thread) exhausted the 60 req/minute bucket at ~23.2s (conc=1), ~11.6s (conc=2), or ~7.7s (conc=3). Even though the Celery worker finished the job in ~28-50s (worker_exec_sec), GET /status/{job_id} kept returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests until the 60.0s SlowAPI rate-limit window expired (~60.0s + ~1.8s setup = ~61.80s-62.11s). (2) With worker_concurrency=2, when 3 jobs are submitted, jobs #1 and #2 run in wave 1 while job #3 waits in the Redis queue (finishing at 87.11s). The P50 (median) of 3 sorted values [61.8s, 61.95s, 87.11s] is the 2nd element (job #2 from wave 1), so P50 at conc=3 only measured wave 1 and hid the queue wait of job #3.
